# Native candidate receipt rehearsal

This fixture exercises the rendered candidate-receipt step through the native dispatcher with a local GitHub and registry. The registry serves a real Cargo archive for an existing crate. The runner must provide the qualified Linux Rust toolchain, mise, and cargo-semver-checks; the fixture does not replace these tools.

For the historical recovery fixture, run `python3 scripts/prepare-gh-fixture-tools.py --with-recovery-fixture` on the Linux x86-64 host before isolating the container. This stages the checksum-verified historical Rust 1.97.1 channel manifest, Velnor 0.1.73 release assets and trusted root in addition to the signed-controller tools. After the command succeeds, use only the complete release set under `recovery-assets/verified`; assemble `/assets` with the other required tools separately and mount it read-only. Verify the release attestations and stage the remaining offline toolchain separately. This staging command does not qualify recovery.

Run `drive.py` inside a network-disabled Linux container with the Velnor checkout at `/src`, this directory at `/fixture`, an empty writable directory at `/workspace`, and writable runner directories at `/runner/<mode>`. Each runner directory needs `velnor/cargo`, `velnor/rustup`, the catalog-qualified `velnor/git-bundle`, and `velnor-semver/cargo-semver-checks`. Install the catalog-qualified Linux Rust 1.99.1 toolchain in the Rustup home and the catalog-pinned checker at that path. The coordinator cases require the corresponding catalog-pinned 1.99.1 channel manifest; they do not prove older Rust or macOS verification. Put the qualified mise and cargo-nextest binaries on `PATH` and populate Cargo's offline dependency cache before starting the container.

Run `python3 /fixture/drive.py success`, then `checksum` and `source`, each with an empty workspace and runner. The success case checks the generated receipt, baseline checksum, and checker identity. The other cases require the exact checksum and changed-source errors without a receipt. Every case checks that the fake services received no mutation.

The test-only entry point leaves the production authority guard enabled. This isolated rehearsal does not test protected GitHub jobs, real OIDC, or publication. Coordinator cases exercise qualified logic only after verifying that the production authority guard rejects the operation.

The `success` case also runs the rendered publisher admission step and requires `release_mode=publish`. The `approval` case gives that step the wrong approval comment; `verify-source` changes source after the receipt is made. Both require an error and no admission output.

The `journal` and `journal-bad-bundle` cases also need `/assets` containing an official Velnor 0.1.73 manifest, its Linux binary and both signed bundles, the catalog-pinned GitHub CLI archive contents, and a public trusted-root file. The test-only runner passes that root to the real `gh attestation verify` command so verification works offline. The positive case verifies the recorded started receipt; the altered bundle must fail before any journal write. These historical assets are test inputs and do not authorize a later generator release.

The `coordinate`, `coordinate-skip`, `coordinate-oidc-denied`, and `coordinate-crash` cases additionally need the catalog-pinned release-plz executable and Rust channel manifest in `/assets`. Run each in a fresh container with network disabled, mapping `api.github.com`, `github.com`, `crates.io`, and `fixture.actions.githubusercontent.com` to `127.0.0.1`. The driver verifies these mappings before running. The real release-plz process uses a Cargo fixture; successful upload cases package the actual source, and registry and OIDC services are local fixtures. The skip case confirms that release-plz reaches the Cargo fixture, the durable upload intent exists, no registry upload occurs, and no completion is recorded. The crash case restarts the coordinator within the same workflow attempt after the fixture receives the archive. It does not prove recovery in a new GitHub run.

The `coordinate-corrupt-git` case modifies the acquired Git bundle and requires rejection before any publication or journal mutation.

The experimental `coordinate-real-cargo-crash` case uses unwrapped Cargo and release-plz, a loopback TLS sparse index, and a local registry that accepts Cargo's framed upload. It requires a network-disabled Linux namespace with only the loopback interface and `index.crates.io` mapped to loopback in addition to the other fixture hosts. It checks a same-attempt process restart after the local registry records the archive; it does not prove recovery in a new GitHub run, live OIDC, or a public release. The production authority guard remains enabled.

The `coordinate-real-cargo-new-run` case uses the same isolated real-Cargo setup. It interrupts run 12 after the local registry accepts one upload, advances to a reviewed fixture policy naming that run as predecessor, and completes repair in run 13. It verifies the predecessor and completion records, the approved source and intent, the archive checksum, the tag, and that no second upload occurred. GitHub, crates.io, and OIDC are simulated; this does not prove a protected GitHub run or live publication.

The `coordinate-evidence-drift` and `coordinate-evidence-checksum-drift` cases use the same real-Cargo, loopback-only setup. Each records START with a genuine checked baseline, then changes only the registry's baseline version or archive checksum when the coordinator starts. They require the explicit evidence-changed error, no operation Intent, no upload attempt, and no further journal or release mutation. `coordinate-evidence-matching` keeps the original baseline and requires the real Intent and completion to retain the checked baseline. These cases generate their baseline archives with Cargo and use the catalog-pinned semver checker and signed generator assets.

The `coordinate-cargo-tamper` case changes one byte in a private copied Cargo executable after START and expects the qualified toolchain verification to reject it before any further journal or registry mutation.

The `coordinate-evidence-deferred` case constructs a two-member workspace in which B depends on an unpublished A. START must record B's evidence as Deferred. After START, the loopback registry exposes A's real Cargo archive; the coordinator must record A's tag and release observations, run the pinned checker for B, record a Checked upload Intent for B, and complete using real Cargo and release-plz. This tests fixture registry behavior, not a public crates.io publication.

The `coordinate-missing-oidc` and `coordinate-missing-bootstrap` cases remove the selected credential and the SemVer checker after journal start. They require a missing-credential error before any upload intent or registry upload. They do not validate an OIDC exchange or token authorization. The `coordinate-crash-no-credentials` case removes OIDC variables on retry after the fixture accepted one upload. It checks that the same run can finish tag and release repair without uploading again.

The coordinator rehearsal is in evidence quarantine because the 2026-11-04 `coordinate` case failed once with an unexplained HTTP transport error. Quarantine does not permit omitting cases or ignoring failures: a protected rehearsal must run the required cases explicitly and block on any failure. Later passes do not resolve the original failure. The upload fixture directly checks the approved source SHA and `src/lib.rs`; coordinator reconciliation performs the full archive comparison.

Supplied-input mode supports a single recovery package on the `main` branch, the `release` environment, crates.io, and a root `Cargo.toml`. Other configurations fail closed. Supplied-input mode does not support the `source`, `checksum`, or `verify-source` fault-injection cases; those cases use the synthetic source.

For offline supplied-source SemVer checks, set `VELNOR_NATIVE_REGISTRY_SNAPSHOT` to a read-only registry snapshot containing exactly `index/` and `cache/`. The test-only runner copies it into a fresh Cargo home with no-follow checks and runs offline. The cache must contain every required crate archive. This setting has no effect in production builds.

Run `rust_cache.py` in a network-disabled Linux container to exercise the real file-by-file Rust verifier with its private archive cache. Supply `/assets/channel.toml` as the catalog-pinned channel manifest and `/assets/rust-archives/<sha256>.tar.xz` for every installed component, downloaded from the authenticated channel. The verifier checks each archive against the channel, rejects a privately corrupted cached archive, and succeeds after restoration. Use the same genuine dedicated Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, and build tools described above.
